hypothesis: If Darwin is right, wholly soft-bodied lineages are almost absent from the fossil record relative to their living diversity, and mineralized-skeleton lineages are heavily over-represented.
pass_criterion: From PBDB occurrences, define soft-bodied phyla (Ctenophora, Nemertea, Platyhelminthes, Nematoda, Gastrotricha, Rotifera, Tardigrada, Onychophora) and mineralized phyla (Mollusca, Brachiopoda, Echinodermata, Bryozoa). Pass if (a) soft-bodied phyla make up <1% of all phylum-assigned PBDB occurrences, AND (b) the fossil-genera-to-extant-genera ratio for soft-bodied phyla is ≤0.1 of the same ratio for mineralized phyla. Extant counts are taken from PBDB's own extant flag (is_extant), so no outside data are needed. The absolute wording "no organism wholly soft can be preserved" is tested separately and is refuted if any such phylum has ≥1 accepted fossil occurrence.
fail_criterion: Fail if soft-bodied phyla make up ≥5% of phylum-assigned occurrences, or if the ratio of their fossil-to-extant genera relative to mineralized phyla is >0.3, so there is no strong preservation bias. The literal "none can be preserved" is also failed by ≥1 accepted occurrence of a wholly soft-bodied phylum, which is expected from Lagerstätten.
interpretation: "Wholly soft" is read as taxa with no mineralized skeleton, using the phylum-level proxy above. "Preserved" means having at least one accepted occurrence in PBDB. "Strongly biased" is read as the under-representation ratios above. The second clause, about shells and bones decaying on non-depositing sea floor, is a taphonomic mechanism. It could only be tested at the collection level via PBDB lithology, environment and taphonomy fields, and is not tested here. Modern reinterpretation: Lagerstätten such as the Burgess Shale and Ediacaran sites show that soft tissue can be preserved, but only rarely. The strict absolute wording therefore probably fails, while the bias reading probably passes.

dataset.name: PBDB Data Service
dataset.why_it_fits: PBDB has an open API that returns fossil occurrences with taxonomic classification, so the proportion of occurrences and genera belonging to soft-bodied versus mineralized phyla can be counted. Fields to use: occs/list with accepted_name, phylum, is_extant, environment, lithology, and taxa/list for genus counts.
